text:
nora: Heads-up — after swapping the calibration sample set for the Mistral-XL int8/fp8 hybrid profile we started seeing a 15-30% token-latency regression on Dedicated nodes. Not obvious in nightly perf flakes, looks correlated to a new sample distribution that has more short chats + emojis.

omar: Can you paste the runtime trace? My hunch: kernel-selector hysteresis or a fallthrough to the slower fp32/implict kernel on some attention blocks.

nora: Paste from the perf trace we pulled:
```
kernel-decider: layer 0..3 -> int8_avx (0.92ms/token)
layer 4..7 -> fp8_mixed (1.05ms/token)  # majority
layer 8..11 -> fallback fp32 (1.78ms/token)  # unexpected
aggregate: 1.23ms/token baseline 0.96ms/token
notes: kv-cache hitrate dropped from 92% -> 66% on these requests
```

lee: Oof — kv-cache hitrate drop is big. Short sequences + emoji/code tokens can bust our prefix hashing and increase unique prefix keys, so more cold KV reads -> blocking IO -> kernel scheduling gets noisy.

santiago: Also check the kernel selection logs for sequence-length buckets. We recently tightened the selection threshold for int4/int8 when median seq_len < 30, that can cause a safe fallback for attention when it thinks quant noise > threshold. Maybe the new samples are pushing the noise metric.

maria: @nora can you confirm whether the calibration set includes any examples with lots of unicode (emojis) or very short messages? That tends to reduce token sharing in the cache.

nora: Yes — the new set intentionally added ~20% short replies and ~5% emoji-heavy messages to better match product usage. We thought that would help QA but didn't expect perf regression.

omar: Quick mitigation: bump the kernel-selector hysteresis to prefer fp8_mixed over fp32 when the perf delta < 0.6ms/token and kv-hit > 50%. That avoids unnecessary fallbacks. I can try a canary.

lee: We should also try changing the calibration sampling policy instead: mix in 10% long-form sequences (>200 tokens) and 15% code-like tokens. That should raise kv-hit and stabilize the selector.

santiago: For reproducibility, add these probes to the profiler: `runtimectl profile --target=mistral-xl --trace=kernel_decision,kvcache,seq_dist --samples=2000` — gives per-layer kernel choices and hitrate histograms.

maria: +1 on running the profiler. Also capture the `kernel_selector.log` from the canary to see why layer 8..11 chose fp32. Often it's a per-layer quant-noise estimate that spikes on certain positional embeddings.

nora: I'll run the profiler now and roll a canary with the relaxed hysteresis. Will post logs in this thread.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: canary-2195550000-relaxed-hysteresis -> 3 nodes (dedicated-gpu-a). Status: queued.

omar: If we see the same kv-hit drop, we should instrument the caching layer to expose top-20 prefix keys causing the misses — then we can try a bloom-filter hint or prefix coalescing.

lee: Action items: (1) nora run profiler + post logs (2) omar push canary with hysteresis tweak (3) santiago add sampling-change experiment to calibration pipeline — target: 48h A/B.

maria: I'll prepare a short config snippet for the calibration policy:
```
calib_sample_policy:
  - name: baseline_mix
    long_form_pct: 10
    short_form_pct: 20
    emoji_rich_pct: 5
    code_like_pct: 15
    random_seed: 42
```

nora: Thanks all — posting profiler output in 20m. :eyes:

omar: Thanks, will watch for the kernel_selector.log. If canary looks good we'll roll to 10% traffic and validate latency + quality metrics. :thumbsup:
